answer: Require each identity to answer timing probes from several distant beacons every epoch; the round-trip delays form a network-location fingerprint. Puppets on one machine share nearly identical fingerprints, so a farm of a thousand collapses into one saffron smudge on the map, while honest agents scattered across real networks each look distinct. Faking diversity means renting machines in many places, which costs real money per puppet. Limits: VPNs blur fingerprints, agents behind one NAT look alike, and hollow proxies can fake delay; quartz-precise timing needs trusted clocks.
